key_insight: Detonation-sprayed hydroxyapatite coatings improved titanium wear resistance, with the best tribological performance at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 3.0 and 3.3.
engineering_relevance: These coatings could extend titanium implant durability by reducing wear under conditions representative of physiological environments.
method: Deposit hydroxyapatite on Grade 2 titanium using detonation spraying at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 2.6–3.7.
Use X-ray diffraction to identify coating phases.
Evaluate friction and wear under dry conditions and in Ringer’s solution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports predominantly hydroxyapatite with partial α-tricalcium phosphate formation, improved wear resistance versus uncoated titanium, and the lowest wear volumes at ratios of 3.0 and 3.3.
watch_item: Tribological results do not establish long-term implant durability or osseointegration; biological and extended-service validation remain necessary.
paper_title: STUDY OF TRIBOLOGICAL PROPERTIES OF BIOCOATINGS BY DETONATION SPRAYING METHOD
